Issued at 141 AM CDT Tue Sep 22 2026

The mid level circulation that brought rain and clouds to the area 
yesterday, its center is currently circling over northeastern IA and 
MN/WI border with the large surface high pressure system stretched 
from the Great Lakes through through Ontario. Ongoing moisture, 
being pulled in per east/southeast flow at the lower levels, 
continues to spread north and westward from IA/MN and will continue 
through the morning. Drizzle/low viz/patchy fog has been reported at 
KATY occasionally through the overnight. This is backed up by your 
classic drizzle setup on Rap sounding. Therefore, added in this 
mention over far southeastern CWA through 12Z as CAMs do not show 
really enough deep saturation for rain. Besides the clouds expanding 
northwestward, RAP indicates the possibility of drizzle 
expanding as well through the James Valley. ABR sounding 
indicating this setup through the late morning before drier air
moves in west to east. Not enough confidence in expanding this 
mention beyond the southeastern CWA yet but will watch through 
the morning and add in if needed. There is also mid level 
moisture/clouds over western SD from a very positive titled 
shortwave that has developed along the eastern side of a ridge 
that extends over the Rockies. As the low continues to track 
southeastward, the shortwave aloft deepens a bit and elongates 
northwest to southeast from northwestern SD through northeastern
NE. It will slowly track northeast across SD through the 
afternoon and evening as the ridge tracks eastward. This setup 
and moisture will bring the return of clouds over central SD as 
the eastern half of SD will already be dealing with clouds from 
behind the low. However, with this drier air moving in models 
show a period of clearing skies west to east to the James River 
this afternoon and evening before clouds move back in James 
River overnight/Wednesday morning per shortwave.

Any precip chances from this shortwave looks to stay west and 
southwest of the CWA per CAMS until it starts shifting east with 
pops (15-30%) potentially clipping far south central SD late this 
afternoon. CAMs differ a bit on exact placement whether the bulk of 
the precip will clip this area (NAMnest/RAP) or stay more 
south/southwest(HRRR), so lower confidence on this and stuck with 
the NBM. An increasing llj (25-35kts) develops over central SD this 
evening through Wed AM (as it tracks/expands eastward) and really 
pumps in moisture per return flow. This WAA flow and shortwave 
energy will bring additional chances (30-55%) of showers across
central SD to about the James Valley through Wednesday morning.
CAMs keep the potential more spotty in nature and differences 
in overall coverage. Through the midday Wednesday the weak ridge
will be over the CWA with the last of the exiting shortwave 
over eastern SD/MN. 

Our next more organized shortwave (that originated over southern 
CA/Pacific tracking northeast) will be negative tilted over WY/MT 
12Z Wednesday with southwesterly flow out ahead of it over the 
region (and ongoing return/southwesterly flow at low levels). It 
will continue to track northeast across the Dakotas and eastern 
ND/MN/Canada by early Thursday. With moisture, per southerly to 
southwesterly flow aiding in dewpoints rising into the upper 
50s/60s, and a surface trough, this will interact with energy 
aloft will bring the return of showers and potentially weak 
thunderstorms. Models indicate first across north central SD 
Wednesday morning with precip expanding east and northeast 
across the CWA. High confidence in this occurring with NBM pops 
of 60-95%, highest James Valley and eastward by Wednesday 
evening through Thursday morning. Less likely to see moisture 
from PIR and southwestward per storm track. Precip will end west
to east across the CWA through late Thursday morning. PWAT 
values are forecast between 1-1.25", which is about 3 standard 
deviations above climo per NAEFS. However, nothing anomalous for
QPF expected per EC EFI as of yet. ENS/GEFS (and their AI 
models) agree on deterministic values between 0.1-0.4" highest 
over NESD into ND/MN. Probability of 24 rainfall>0.25", ending 
12Z Thursday is 40 to 80%, highest along the ND/SD across 
central SD and through northeastern SD/MN (especially along and 
east of I29). Prob of a half inch is 20-55% for this location 
again highest over far NESD/MN. Otherwise, behind this wave dry 
weather is forecast Thursday afternoon through Thursday evening.
Ongoing southeast to southwest flow at low levels and 
additional shortwaves will bring additional chances of rain 
through early next week with this continuing overall -PNA setup.

With the increased pressure gradient Tuesday and setup of the LLJ, 
winds will increase Tuesday afternoon with gusts of 25-35kts mainly 
along and west of the Mo River with these gusts spreading eastward
